Electromagnetic wave absorbing materials (EWAMs) reduce radar detection by absorbing incident electromagnetic energy but are limited by coating thickness, incident wave angles, and working frequencies.
Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) are planar arrays of passive elements that can independently manipulate the amplitude and phase of incident electromagnetic waves.
The proposed IRS-aided ES system deploys IRS on the target surface alongside EWAMs to synergistically reduce radar echo signals.
The system model assumes a uniform planar array (UPA) with N = N1 + N2 elements, where N1 are IRS elements and N2 are EWAM elements.
The radar is modeled as a monostatic system with a uniform planar array of M active antennas.
The received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the radar is expressed as a function of the IRS reflection matrix and EWAM reflection matrix.
The optimization problem minimizes the radar received SNR subject to modulus constraints on IRS reflection coefficients.
The problem is convex and solved using Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions to obtain a semi-closed-form solution.
Simulation results show that increasing the number of IRS elements from 1 to 70 dramatically decreases the received SNR at the radar.
The IRS-aided system achieves perfect stealth performance (SNR approaches zero) when the number of IRS elements exceeds a threshold (e.g., N ≥ 20).
Random phase shift IRS designs perform worse than no-IRS designs in terms of received SNR due to lack of destructive signal combination.
The absorbing efficiency p of EWAM elements ranges from 0 to 1 and directly affects the received SNR at the radar.
The IRS-aided system outperforms amplitude-control-only IRS designs due to enhanced flexibility from phase control.
The system assumes far-field line-of-sight (LoS) channels with Doppler effects due to target motion.
The cross-shaped sensing array embedded in the ES surface enables angle-of-arrival estimation for IRS reflection optimization.
The optimization dual problem can be reformulated as a semidefinite programming (SDP) problem solvable with standard SDP solvers.
The computational complexity of the SDP approach is O(N^4.5), which motivates the semi-closed-form solution.
The system can precompute IRS reflection coefficients offline for different AoA conditions to enable real-time adaptation.
The Neyman-Pearson criterion is used for radar detection decision-making based on received signal statistics.
The IRS reflection coefficients are complex values with amplitude ≤ 1 and phase in [0, 2π).
The proposed IRS-aided ES system is validated through simulations comparing it to no-IRS and random phase IRS baselines.
